title: Prefetch Playbook Canvas — interactive recommendations & guardrails for caching + batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an interactive Prefetch Playbook Canvas inside the Redwood Console that surfaces tailored caching + batching recommendations, explains trade-offs (cost vs latency vs quality), and provides safe rollout/guardrail controls. The canvas should combine prescriptive 'policy cards', a lightweight simulator for expected token cost and p95 latency across common workload archetypes, and clear rollback/canary controls for operators. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype of the canvas, developer-facing component spec, and a short usability script for a 20-minute design review with PM/Eng.
acceptance_criteria: A Figma prototype covers three entry points: Quick Preset (1-click), Guided Tuner (wizard), and Advanced JSON policy editor
Simulator runs 3 workload archetypes (chatty assistant, short completions, high-throughput embeddings) and shows estimated cost and p95 latency for current and proposed policies
Each recommendation card includes rationale, estimated savings, risk level, and an explicit fallback suggestion
Rollout controls include canary toggle, traffic % slider, automatic rollback trigger with readable reason, and audit trail link
Design tokens and accessibility checks (contrast, keyboard nav) are documented in the component spec
PM and two engineering reviewers have signed off on handoff notes and API contract examples
decision_log: 2026-02-28 — Decided to keep defaults conservative: Quick Preset favors reliability over maximum token savings to reduce support burden
2026-03-02 — Chose simulator inputs: base latency distribution + prefix hit rates from telemetry sample (Q4 2025), not synthetic extremes
2026-03-06 — Opted for a hybrid UX: policy cards for discovery + JSON editor for advanced users to preserve power-user workflows
review_feedback: Priya Patel (PM): Add explicit customer examples to each recommendation card (e.g., 'Works best for chatbots with stable prompts')
Diego Alvarez (Eng): Simulator should surface confidence bands and note assumptions; do not promise exact cost numbers
Anika Rao (SRE): Guardrail UI must include audit log link and a human-readable rollback reason; default rollback triggers need to be conservative
Accessibility review (Maya): Ensure traffic % slider is operable via keyboard and provides current value announcement for screen readers
